Peer selection and scoring logic with pools, maps, treaps, and cluster slot updates.

# Purpose
`fd_sspeer_selector.c` implements a peer selection component for a snapshot service. It stores peers by IPv4 address and port, tracks each peer `latency`, `ssinfo`, and computed `score`, and keeps the peers in three internal data structures: a pool for object storage, a chained map for address lookup, and a treap ordered by score. The file also defines the memory layout and lifecycle functions for the selector object, including [`fd_sspeer_selector_align`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_align>), [`fd_sspeer_selector_footprint`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_footprint>), [`fd_sspeer_selector_new`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_new>), [`fd_sspeer_selector_join`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_join>), [`fd_sspeer_selector_leave`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_leave>), and [`fd_sspeer_selector_delete`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_delete>).

The selector API lets callers add, update, remove, and query peers. [`fd_sspeer_selector_score`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_score>) computes a peer score from latency and slot lag, [`fd_sspeer_selector_best`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_best>) returns the best peer that matches the current snapshot state, and [`fd_sspeer_selector_process_cluster_slot`](<#fd_sspeer_selector_process_cluster_slot>) updates the cluster slot state and rescales all peers when the cluster advances. The file also supports incremental snapshot fetch mode through `incremental_snapshot_fetch`, and it uses a shadow treap plus a peer index list to rebuild the score order after a cluster slot update.
